chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya al-Ijli, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The thunderbolts will not strike a dhakir (one who remembers Allah).' I said, 'And what is the dhakir?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who recites one hundred verses.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a 'Zakir' in this hadith and what is the benefit of this practice?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (as), defining a 'dhakir' specifically as one who recites one hundred verses of the Quran, thereby linking this specific act of worship to divine protection from calamities like thunderbolts. This hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on the quantitative and qualitative aspects of dhikr as a means of spiritual safeguarding, reflecting the broader theological view that consistent remembrance fortifies the believer against both physical and metaphysical harms.
